title: Apply for a new PAN card
summary: A PAN card is used for tax and many financial records in India. This guide explains the basic application flow and the points a user should confirm on the official PAN portal before submitting.
documents_needed: Recent photograph if required by the selected application flow

steps.title: Open an official PAN application portal
steps.detail: Use the official Protean/NSDL or UTIITSL PAN service. Avoid agent websites unless you deliberately choose paid help.

steps.title: Choose the correct application type
steps.detail: Select the option for a new PAN and the applicant category that matches the user, such as individual Indian citizen.

steps.title: Enter details consistently
steps.detail: Names, date of birth, and address should match the supporting documents. Mismatches can cause rejection or delay.

steps.title: Submit identity and address documents
steps.detail: Upload or provide documents using the method supported by the official portal. Keep scans clear and readable.

steps.title: Pay only through the official payment flow
steps.detail: Check the current official fee on the portal before payment because fees and delivery options can change.

steps.title: Save the acknowledgement
steps.detail: Keep the acknowledgement number or receipt so the application can be tracked later.

warnings.title: Confirm the latest official form and fee
warnings.message: PAN application forms, portals, and fees can change. Confirm the latest requirement on the official portal before submitting.

warnings.title: Avoid sharing real ID data in the demo
warnings.message: During project development, use only fake examples. Do not upload real PAN, Aadhaar, address, or bank details.

title: File your Income Tax Return (ITR) - basics
summary: Income Tax Return filing is done through the Income Tax Department e-filing portal. This guide explains the basic user flow and reminds users to confirm the current assessment year, form, deadline, and e-verification rules on the official portal.
documents_needed: Form 16 for salaried users if available
Investment and deduction proofs if claiming deductions

steps.title: Open the Income Tax e-filing portal
steps.detail: Use the official Income Tax Department portal and sign in with the correct taxpayer account.

steps.title: Choose the correct assessment year and form
steps.detail: The form depends on the user's income type and situation. A salaried person may often use ITR-1, but this must be confirmed.

steps.title: Review pre-filled information
steps.detail: Check income, tax deducted, bank details, and deductions. Do not assume pre-filled data is always complete.

steps.title: Submit and e-verify
steps.detail: Submission is not the end of the process. The return must also be verified using an allowed method.

steps.title: Save acknowledgement
steps.detail: Download the acknowledgement or ITR-V and keep it for records.

warnings.title: Deadline changes must be checked live
warnings.message: Filing deadlines can be extended or changed. Confirm the current deadline on the official Income Tax portal before relying on any date.

warnings.title: E-verification is required
warnings.message: If a filed return is not verified within the required time, it may not be treated as valid. Confirm the current rule on the official portal.

title: Understand a loan agreement
summary: A loan agreement explains the borrower, lender, amount, interest rate, repayment schedule, fees, default consequences, and complaint process. This guide helps users identify clauses worth checking before signing or asking a bank officer.

steps.title: Check amount, tenure, and interest type
steps.detail: Confirm the principal amount, loan duration, and whether the rate is fixed, floating, or mixed.

steps.title: Read the EMI schedule
steps.detail: Confirm the EMI amount, due date, number of instalments, and total repayment amount.

steps.title: Find penalty and default clauses
steps.detail: Look for late payment charges, penal charges, and consequences of default. Ask the lender to explain exact amounts and triggers.

steps.title: Check prepayment and foreclosure terms
steps.detail: Some loans have restrictions or charges for early repayment. Rules differ by loan type, lender type, and rate type.

steps.title: List all fees and add-ons
steps.detail: Processing fees, documentation charges, insurance, and other add-ons should be clear before signing.

steps.title: Find the complaint process
steps.detail: The agreement or lender website should explain how to raise complaints and escalate unresolved issues.

warnings.title: Late payment and penal charges
warnings.message: Penalty terms can significantly increase cost. Ask when the charge applies, how it is calculated, and whether taxes or extra charges apply.

warnings.title: Prepayment and foreclosure conditions
warnings.message: Do not assume early repayment is free. Check the exact clause and ask the lender how it applies to this loan type.

warnings.title: Bundled products
warnings.message: If insurance or other products are bundled with the loan, ask whether they are optional and how they affect total cost.

source.name: Reserve Bank of India consumer and fair practices materials
